# Generated evidence: morpho/vault-deposit

Written by `pnpm report morpho/vault-deposit --instance-of steakhouse-prime-usdc-v2-0f51 --record` from `templates/morpho/vault-deposit/template.json`, `templates/morpho/vault-deposit/docs.json`, `templates/morpho/vault-deposit/instances/steakhouse-prime-usdc-v2-0f51/docs.json`, `registry/contracts.json`, `testdata/report/morpho-vault-deposit/steakhouse-prime-usdc-v2-0f51.json`, `testdata/abi`, `testdata/research/morpho-vault-deposit-steakhouse-prime-usdc-v2-0f51.json`. The listings and pages were read on 2026-11-26. `pnpm test` computes it again from these files and fails on any difference: every section is recomputed from the recorded answers except the vault evidence, which is stored as `pnpm instance-evidence` printed it. The recordings were made on the AI's computer, and no program reads their answers live again. Text from outside the program appears only as identifiers: a contract name Etherscan gives, printed only when it is a Solidity identifier, and the file paths, field paths and format names `pnpm erc7730` prints. The URLs come from the registry and `docs.json`, in RFC 3986 characters only. Text the AI wrote appears only where a row says it was written by the AI in the template. Do not edit this file.

## Official documentation

Each page comes from `docs.json`, whose contract must be the one the template calls the function on when the template binds it. The program compares the page's registrable domain, or GitHub organization, with the DefiLlama protocol that contract belongs to, its factory's for an entry a factory deploys, checks that a GitHub page is pinned to a commit on the default branch, and looks in the page as served, without scripts, for the function's name written as code: directly followed by `(`, between backticks, or alone as a block, such as a heading, a list item or a table cell. A PASS there shows that the page names a function of that name, not that it documents this contract's function. A function a token standard defines may instead name that standard: its page, the GitHub org that publishes it and the function's declaration are held by the program, the page must hold that declaration, and its org is compared with the standard's, not with the contract's protocol. Such a PASS shows that the standard defines the function, not that this contract follows the standard.
